brief: A Zero Hedge write-up relaying Goldman Sachs derivatives head Brian Garrett, who says he made an attempt to be balanced but flags non-fundamental headwinds stocks must digest in the near term. Short term CTA thresholds on NDX, SPX and RTY all broke this morning, on top of a European index that broke down earlier in the week. Modelled supply is -23bn over one week and -28bn over one month, and that does not incorporate the pre-market sell-off. VIX tends to be around 25 when this type of technical deterioration happens and is currently 17. Gamma at spot is still supportive because the street is long, but the desk models a flip from positive to negative on a further selloff of roughly 200bps. Global systematic positioning across CTA, vol control and risk parity is estimated at $421 billion, close to five-year highs, and seasonals are ugly, so cheap protection is being bought and stocks are tracking oil inverted. The write-up's own translation: mechanical sellers are already activated, volatility is priced too calmly, systematic money is still long, and the next few sessions are a digestion period rather than a clean fundamental story.
